seismic_rule: decided by SWBPIPE Agent 0 on 2026-11-12, in DEL-05-01's wording: for each global axis, the g-factor times the weight the weight case gives the model: on every member a load per length a * g * mu; for a member whose component weight the weight case applies, in place of that load, the force a * W at the component's node with its moments about the node from the centre-of-gravity vector; a member whose component weight the weight case does not apply keeps its distributed load. Which component weights the weight case applies is the specification's (§5, §8.1: component weights at their centres of gravity in place of their members' distributed weight): RS-F1, RS-V1, RS-F2 in both systems and RS-R1 in the full system; RS-R1 is pending in the fixture today (§10), where RS-P150 keeps its distributed weight and so its distributed seismic load. Convention (SWBPIPE Agent 0): the self-weight plan evaluated at the seismic case's gravity, with each entered component force W held fixed; it names an exception and does not make the two mass models equivalent in general. This closes the former open reading OR-1.
specification_observations: sense of a positive g-factor: taken along the positive global axis; the opposite sense (for Z, along gravity) reverses every seismic force and moment
RS-P150 carries section S270 (§3.2) under the reducer RS-R1 (270 to 220 mm): its wind diameter, and its distributed seismic load in the fixture today, use S270

open_readings.subject: the seismic case's gravity magnitude
open_readings.status: open: §2 says the seismic case enters gravity_acceleration explicitly but gives no value, and the lane that holds the specification is adding it to §8.1. Every seismic value here is conditional on the stated assumption 9.80665 m/s^2 (the weight case's gravity). The distributed part of the seismic weight scales with g and the component forces W do not, so another value would move each seismic value, but not in simple proportion. No alternative values are frozen. Nothing else in the specification is left open for these references.
